title: Block anonymous hands and hand-object intersections
starting_state: A doorway slide contains an extra hand entering from the door edge with no owner or story purpose.
A moving-box slide has the correct number of people and hands, but a forearm passes through the solid box wall.
done_when: Every visible hand has an owner, side, story purpose, wrist/forearm attachment, and concrete contact/occlusion evidence.
An unexplained edge-entry hand blocks approval even when the people count is correct.
A hand or forearm intersecting a solid object blocks approval even when hand count and finger count are correct.
forbidden_changes: Do not treat correct finger count as sufficient anatomy QA.
Do not allow an unattributed hand because it looks aesthetically plausible.
Do not accept a grip or support pose without checking solid-object boundaries and overlap order.
fail_to_pass: the anonymous door-edge hand and the forearm-through-box fixture are both rejected
pass_to_pass: a narratively required, owned hand with continuous anatomy and believable object contact passes
anti_gaming_notes: Hidden variants should use an arm through a container rim, an anonymous hand at a frame edge, a hand emerging from clothing, an impossible load-bearing grip, and a valid partially occluded hand control case.
